definitions.explanation: A local branch of the National Tax Agency that handles income tax returns, tax audits, and other tax-related matters. There are over 500 tax offices across Japan.

examples.japanese: {税務署|ぜいむしょ}に{確定申告|かくていしんこく}を{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To file a tax return at the tax office.

examples.japanese: {税務署|ぜいむしょ}から{通知|つうち}が{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: A notice arrived from the tax office.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{二月|にがつ}から{三月|さんがつ}にかけて、{税務署|ぜいむしょ}は{確定申告|かくていしんこく}の{相談|そうだん}で{混雑|こんざつ}する。
examples.english: Every year from February to March, tax offices are crowded with people seeking help with their tax returns.

notes:
USAGE:
{税務署|ぜいむしょ} is the local branch where individuals and small businesses interact with the tax system. It is distinct from the {国税庁|こくぜいちょう} (National Tax Agency), which is the central authority.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {税務署|ぜいむしょ}に{届|とど}け{出|で}る: to file/report to the tax office
- {税務署|ぜいむしょ}に{相談|そうだん}する: to consult the tax office
- {税務署|ぜいむしょ}の{窓口|まどぐち}: tax office counter
- {税務署|ぜいむしょ}の{調査|ちょうさ}: tax office audit

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, the tax filing season ({確定申告|かくていしんこく}) runs from February 16 to March 15 each year. Many people visit their local {税務署|ぜいむしょ} in person, though online filing (e-Tax) is increasingly common.
